label: 23 August 1939
title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
summary: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a nonaggression pact. A secret protocol sets out spheres of influence in eastern Europe, including a proposed division of Poland.

label: 1 September 1939
title: Germany invades Poland
summary: German forces invade Poland, beginning the war in Europe. This date marks the invasion, not a completed occupation or a change in Polish sovereignty.

label: 17 September 1939
title: The Soviet Union invades eastern Poland
summary: The Red Army invades Poland from the east. Soviet claims that the intervention was protective were official justifications, not a description adopted by this atlas.

label: 28 September 1939
title: German–Soviet Boundary and Friendship Treaty
summary: Germany and the Soviet Union sign a treaty revising their territorial arrangements for occupied Poland. The map shows an approximate trace of the agreed partition, not a reconstructed military front.

label: 26 October 1939
title: German occupation administration takes shape
summary: Germany formally annexes several occupied Polish regions and places other German-occupied areas under the General Government. Eastern Poland remained under Soviet occupation; formal Soviet incorporation measures followed later. These acts did not establish recognized Polish consent or sovereignty.
dateRationale: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum identifies 26 October as the date of German annexations and establishment of the General Government civilian administration.
